headline: Bangladesh outraged over India allowing Hasina's media interaction in New Delhi
summary: The Foreign Ministry states that allowing the former PM to speak is an insult to the July Revolution martyrs and a blow to bilateral ties.
details: Bangladesh has expressed deep outrage after India allowed former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to interact directly with the media in New Delhi. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the move as a violation of Bangladesh's sovereignty.
In a statement issued Wednesday, the ministry said Hasina and her associates used the platform to make 'poisonous' remarks against the state and the people of Bangladesh.

The government noted that India was previously informed about the potential negative impact such an event could have on the process of rebuilding bilateral relations, yet the interaction was still permitted.
The ministry termed the event a 'failed attempt' to rewrite history, especially as the people of Bangladesh mark the anniversary of the July Revolution.
It emphasized that Hasina and her circle have no place in the politics of Bangladesh, now or in the future, following the atrocities committed during the July-August period.
Bangladesh also highlighted that India has not responded to repeated requests for the extradition of Hasina under the 2013 extradition treaty signed between the two nations.
The statement concluded that allowing her to speak publicly under any pretext deeply hurts the sentiments of the Bangladeshi people and is detrimental to the development of friendly bilateral ties.

headline: Petrol bomb hurled at Sakin Al Hasan's house in Magura
summary: Attackers hurled a petrol bomb and cocktails cocktails at the gate of the former cricket captain's residence on Wednesday night.
details: Attackers hurled a petrol bomb and cocktails at the gate of the residence of Shakib Al Hasan, a former MP and former captain of the Bangladesh national cricket team, in Magura.
The incident occurred on Wednesday night at the Keshav Mor intersection in Magura.
Police reported that an explosive-like object was thrown at the upper part of the iron gate on the south side of the house, causing a fire.
The fire was extinguished shortly after the attack, and no major damage or injuries were reported.
A team from the Magura Sadar Police Station arrived at the scene following the report and has deployed police personnel for security.
Police stated that there is currently no information regarding the identity of the perpetrators. An investigation is ongoing to determine the cause of the attack and the nature of the explosive used.
